paragraphs: The paper introduces resources for studying whether video models can reason about events, rather than assessing only how convincing their images look. The target abilities include understanding continuity, interactions, and causal relationships across space and time. These abilities require tracking how a visual situation develops, which makes video a useful setting for studying reasoning.

The Very Big Video Reasoning dataset contains more than one million clips covering 200 curated reasoning tasks, organized through a systematic taxonomy. The authors describe it as roughly a thousand times larger than existing datasets. This scale addresses a practical obstacle: studying how reasoning changes with training scale requires substantial training data across different kinds of problems.

The accompanying VBVR-Bench uses rule-based scorers aligned with human judgments to make evaluation reproducible and easier to interpret. Using the suite, the authors observe early signs of generalization to reasoning tasks absent from training. That finding is preliminary evidence of emerging transfer, rather than a claim that general video reasoning has been achieved.
icml-2026-a-very-big-video-reasoning-sui.tldr: VBVR supplies large-scale training data and rule-based evaluation for video reasoning, with early evidence of generalization to unseen tasks.

paragraphs: An assistant helping with visual design needs to clarify what a user wants, but each question also demands effort. This paper treats that effort as part of the design problem. Its A-MPQC framework aims to improve the final design while reducing user interaction burden as estimated by a proxy.

The method plans sequences of clarification questions and revises those plans as the conversation progresses. This receding-horizon approach lets the assistant consider how an early question could reduce ambiguity later, while still adapting after receiving new information. A lightweight reward based on whether a user would respond or reject a question encourages formats expected to be easier to answer, such as yes/no questions.

On webpage and advertising-banner generation benchmarks, the framework produces designs better aligned with user intent and lower measured interaction costs than the tested baselines. Those comparisons include fixed question formats and a retrieval-augmented approach. The method operates without retraining, showing how planning at interaction time can improve both design alignment and proxy-estimated conversational effort.
icml-2026-agentic-model-predictive-quest.tldr: A-MPQC plans and revises clarification questions to improve visual designs while reducing proxy-estimated user effort.

paragraphs: Some deepfake detectors learn what real content looks like so they can recognize unfamiliar forgeries. This paper identifies a possible weakness in representing real content as a continuous space: smooth interpolation may also accommodate artifacts produced by generative models. That can blur the distinction the detector is meant to preserve.

The proposed method introduces a learned vector-quantized codebook into the feature space of a CLIP vision encoder. The codebook represents real content through discrete alternatives, creating a tighter information bottleneck. The intended effect is to reduce the likelihood that generative artifacts fit comfortably inside the learned representation of real data.

Strict discreteness also needs flexibility to generalize. The authors therefore add an adaptive tangent-space projection that permits a controlled continuous relaxation around the discrete representation. Together, the components aim to constrain the real-data distribution while allowing useful variation. Experiments across diverse datasets support the method’s effectiveness and robustness to unseen forgeries; the mechanism reduces an identified risk rather than guaranteeing that every forgery will be excluded.
icml-2026-breaking-manifold-continuity-v.tldr: The method combines discrete real-image representations with controlled continuous flexibility to improve detection of unseen deepfakes.

paragraphs: Pansharpening combines a sharp panchromatic image with a lower-resolution multispectral image. The challenge is to bring together fine spatial detail and spectral information. Fourier-based methods help by exposing frequency components and global relationships, but the authors argue that common processing operations overlook the special organization of this frequency representation.

In that representation, each coordinate corresponds to a particular frequency, and energy is distributed unevenly, generally decreasing outward. ABFNet adapts the classical Butterworth filter to work directly with this structure. Its filters are learnable and direction-dependent, allowing the network to select different frequency content along different orientations instead of applying the same filtering behavior in every direction.

A dual-branch gating module combines this adaptive selection with global context and local details at linear complexity. The authors report state-of-the-art pansharpening results with low computational overhead. They also report superior accuracy on CIFAR-100 classification, providing evidence that the frequency-processing approach can be useful beyond image fusion, rather than establishing effectiveness across all vision tasks.
icml-2026-butterworth-as-attention-aniso.tldr: ABFNet uses learnable, direction-aware Butterworth filters to fuse images efficiently in the frequency domain.

paragraphs: This paper studies how a deep residual model develops a prediction across its layers. Viewing the forward pass as a discretized continuous flow makes intermediate representations part of a trajectory. Conventional training mainly constrains the final prediction, leaving much of the trajectory without direct supervision.

The authors formalize this process as a conditional discriminative flow and examine it using Tuned Lens analysis. They find that semantic evidence accumulates according to an exponential schedule: an extended period of feature construction precedes a rapid move toward confident classification in later layers. This observed progression motivates supervising intermediate layers in a way that respects their stage of development.

Deep Trajectory Supervision adds auxiliary training signals aligned with that exponential pattern. Its purpose is to guide the evolution of representations, rather than treating intermediate states as interchangeable points along the network. Evaluations on ImageNet-1K and other benchmarks show significantly faster convergence and improved final performance. These results support the value of matching supervision to the measured progression of evidence through model depth.
icml-2026-deep-trajectory-supervision-de.tldr: Deep Trajectory Supervision improves training by aligning intermediate supervision with the observed exponential buildup of semantic evidence.

paragraphs: Federated learning combines updates from clients whose data can differ substantially. A shared model may consequently work well for some clients and poorly for others. FedEBA+ addresses the difficulty of reducing these performance disparities while preserving the accuracy of the global model.

The framework combines two mechanisms. First, it uses the maximum entropy principle to derive a closed-form expression for aggregation weights, determining how client contributions are combined to promote fairness. Second, a step-wise alignment procedure synchronizes gradient directions across clients. This alignment targets the drift caused by local training on heterogeneous data, complementing the fairness-oriented weighting.

The paper provides convergence analysis covering non-convex settings and extends its analysis of performance variation to generalized regression. Experiments on five datasets show better fairness than the compared state-of-the-art methods without sacrificing global accuracy. The contribution therefore joins an aggregation rule, a mechanism for coordinating local updates, and theoretical analysis, with empirical evidence that fairness and accuracy can improve together in the evaluated settings.
icml-2026-fedeba-towards-fair-and-effect.tldr: FedEBA+ combines entropy-derived aggregation weights and client-update alignment to improve fairness while preserving global accuracy.

paragraphs: FIPN is a forecasting model whose structure grows one layer at a time. Instead of optimizing the entire network through backpropagation, it generates candidate components, estimates their parameters in closed form, and selects them using validation performance. This construction makes the learned structure more accessible for tracing how forecasts are produced.

Each neuron combines a fuzzy rule with a polynomial prediction component enhanced by Fourier functions. Fuzzy clustering assigns inputs softly to local regimes, producing interpretable rule weights. The prediction component keeps access to original features while using Fourier functions to represent periodic and frequency-related patterns. These pieces connect local rules to the temporal structures needed for forecasting.

Adding layers can introduce redundant components, correlated features, and overfitting. FIPN addresses those risks through regularized node scoring, dropout-based redundancy control, and continued access to raw inputs. On long-horizon forecasting benchmarks, it achieves competitive accuracy with a compact model. Its learned rules also provide explanations at both the rule and architectural levels, supporting the authors’ proposed balance of accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability.
icml-2026-fipn-forward-self-organizing-i.tldr: FIPN grows interpretable forecasting networks without backpropagation, combining fuzzy rules, polynomial predictions, and Fourier features.

paragraphs: GradPower changes the gradient supplied to an optimizer during language-model pretraining. For each gradient component, it preserves the sign and raises the absolute magnitude to a fixed positive power. The transformed gradient then enters the existing optimizer, leaving that optimizer’s internal logic and hyperparameters unchanged.

This makes the intervention small in implementation: the authors describe it as a single-line code change. Applied to AdamW, the resulting AdamWPower method consistently reaches lower final training loss across the tested architectures, datasets, model sizes, and learning-rate schedules. The evaluations include LLaMA and Qwen2MoE models, scales from 66 million to 2 billion parameters, and C4 and OpenWebText data.

The largest reported gains occur for modern mixture-of-experts models trained with warmup-stable-decay schedules. GradPower also improves results when combined with Muon, indicating usefulness beyond AdamW in the reported experiments. The paper supplies theoretical analysis of the transformation’s mechanism and the role of gradient noise, connecting a simple implementation change with its observed training benefits.
icml-2026-gradpower-powering-gradients-f.tldr: GradPower applies a simple sign-preserving power transformation to gradients and improves final pretraining loss across tested models and optimizers.

paragraphs: Sequential stochastic combinatorial optimization involves choosing among enormous action spaces while handling uncertainty, long-term consequences, and limited resources. Hierarchical reinforcement learning can organize decisions into larger actions, but those actions may last different amounts of time. That variability complicates the world model used to predict outcomes and plan ahead.

The proposed framework combines tree search in a learned latent space with a world model designed for variable-duration decisions. A multi-timescale training objective makes the magnitude of latent transitions reflect the effective temporal scale of abstract actions. The planner can therefore look ahead using abstractions whose durations adapt, while the representation explicitly accounts for those differences.

The method also learns a budget policy conditioned on the current subgoal, jointly with the world model. This supports allocating resources according to the decision context. Across challenging benchmarks, the framework outperforms strong baselines. The results support treating temporal abstraction, predictive modeling, and resource allocation as connected parts of hierarchical planning, rather than leaving action duration implicit in the learned dynamics.
icml-2026-learning-multi-timescale-abstr.tldr: The framework improves hierarchical combinatorial planning by modeling variable action durations and learning context-dependent resource budgets.

paragraphs: Generating a convincing human-object interaction requires both natural movement and accurate physical contact. The authors identify a problem they call geometric forgetting: deeper diffusion-model features increasingly emphasize semantic intent while losing information about the object’s geometry. A generated action can consequently express the intended interaction while failing to maintain precise contact.

MaMi-HOI addresses this through two adapters with complementary roles. The Geometry-Aware Proximity Adapter reinserts detailed object information and applies residual corrections to improve contact. However, strong local corrections can make the resulting movement stiff. The Kinematic Harmony Adapter therefore adjusts whole-body posture to accommodate those spatial requirements as part of the overall motion.

The framework coordinates local geometric precision with global movement instead of relying on contact corrections alone. Experiments show that it achieves both natural motion and accurate contact. The authors also demonstrate generation of longer tasks with complex trajectories, extending the approach to interactions that combine movement through a scene with detailed object manipulation. This connects whole-body navigation and local contact within the same generation framework.
icml-2026-mami-hoi-harmonizing-global-ki.tldr: MaMi-HOI coordinates detailed contact corrections with whole-body posture adjustments to generate natural, precise human-object interactions.

paragraphs: This paper addresses a tension in safety training for reasoning models: teaching rules can interfere with useful reasoning when the model develops a rigid connection between recalling a rule and refusing a request. The authors identify this problem in approaches that embed explicit safety rules into chain-of-thought training data through context distillation.

Adaptive Safe Context Learning turns safety alignment into a multi-turn tool-use process. The model learns when to consult safety rules and how to continue reasoning with the resulting context. Separating consultation from subsequent reasoning gives the model a decision to make about obtaining relevant guidance, instead of binding rule retrieval directly to refusal.

Reinforcement learning can still create a preference for consulting rules. To counter that tendency, the authors introduce Inverse Frequency Policy Optimization, which rebalances advantage estimates used in policy training. The combined framework achieves higher overall performance than the compared baselines. The stated result supports adaptive rule consultation as a way to mitigate the safety–utility trade-off, without claiming that the trade-off disappears.
icml-2026-mitigating-the-safetyutility-t.tldr: ASCL teaches reasoning models when to retrieve safety rules and how to reason afterward, improving overall performance against tested baselines.

paragraphs: A cyclic peptide can adopt multiple ring-shaped structures, making a single deterministic prediction inadequate for capturing its conformational variety. MuCO models a distribution of cyclic structures conditioned on the corresponding linear peptide. The goal is to support computational exploration of candidate peptides whose physical and pharmaceutical properties depend on structure.

The method separates cyclization into three stages. It first designs the backbone with attention to ring topology, then generates side-chain arrangements, and finally performs physics-aware optimization of all atoms. This coarse-to-fine organization handles the broad structural arrangement before refining the complete molecular configuration. It also supports parallel sampling to explore diverse low-energy structures efficiently.

On the large-scale CPSea dataset, MuCO significantly and consistently outperforms the compared state-of-the-art methods in physical stability, structural diversity, secondary-structure recovery, and computational efficiency. Those results support its use as a computational tool for exploring and designing cyclic peptides. The reported achievements concern generated conformations and their evaluated properties, rather than demonstrated pharmaceutical performance of resulting candidates.
icml-2026-muco-generative-peptide-cycliz.tldr: MuCO generates diverse cyclic-peptide structures through backbone design, side-chain generation, and physics-aware all-atom refinement.

paragraphs: An agent reasoning over retrieved images and videos can accumulate a long history that consumes many tokens while containing relatively little useful evidence. VimRAG addresses this problem by organizing agent states and retrieved material into a changing directed acyclic graph. The graph provides structured memory across text, images, and videos.

Its visual-memory encoding mechanism uses a node’s position in the graph to assess its significance. Important evidence receives more high-resolution tokens, while less useful clues are compressed or discarded. This makes the allocation of visual detail depend on how evidence participates in the reasoning structure, rather than simply retaining everything in a linear interaction history.

The framework also introduces graph-guided policy optimization. By pruning memory nodes linked to redundant actions, it separates the validity of individual steps from rewards assigned to the complete reasoning trajectory. This supports more precise credit assignment during training. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance across diverse multimodal retrieval-augmented generation benchmarks, supporting structured memory as a useful basis for both context management and policy learning.
icml-2026-navigating-massive-visual-cont.tldr: VimRAG uses a graph of reasoning states and evidence to allocate visual tokens and improve learning from multimodal retrieval.

paragraphs: This paper asks when physical parameters can be uniquely recovered from video, focusing on time-invariant second-order linear differential equations. The objective is structural identifiability: determining whether the observations contain enough information to distinguish the underlying parameters. The proposed pipeline uses an encoder without reconstructing the original pixels.

The authors prove that a level-set slope-coverage condition is sufficient to make the learned latent representation locally affine to the true physical state, enabling exact parameter recovery. Their theory also distinguishes data requirements across damping regimes. Within the analyzed setting, underdamped systems can be identified from a single video clip, whereas other regimes require three diverse trajectories. These claims belong to the stated model class and theoretical conditions.

A variance-floor regularizer stabilizes training by preventing the latent representation from collapsing. Experiments on synthetic and real-world data demonstrate reliable estimation of interpretable physical constants. Together, the theory and experiments support extracting physical parameters directly from visual representations, avoiding the computational expense of a pixel-reconstruction objective.
icml-2026-physics-from-video-identifiabi.tldr: The paper establishes conditions for recovering second-order linear physical laws from video using an encoder without pixel reconstruction.

paragraphs: Block-sparse attention can accelerate the processing of long prompts by computing attention only for selected blocks. Choosing those blocks can itself be expensive. Prism addresses why inexpensive block summaries sometimes miss important attention patterns, forcing existing methods to return to costly token-level scoring.

The authors trace the problem to the interaction between mean pooling and rotary positional embeddings. Their analysis shows that averaging behaves like a low-pass filter: high-frequency dimensions can interfere destructively, weakening signals that carry local positional information. Prism separates block selection into high- and low-frequency branches, then uses energy-based temperature calibration to restore attenuated positional signals from the pooled representations.

Because the selection process operates entirely at block level, it avoids the token-level searching that can undermine sparse attention’s efficiency. The method requires no training. Evaluations report accuracy parity with full attention and speedups of up to 5.1 times. These findings show that accounting for positional frequency structure can improve block selection while preserving accuracy in the tested settings.
icml-2026-prism-spectral-aware-block-spa.tldr: Prism corrects frequency-related distortions in pooled attention summaries to select sparse blocks efficiently without training.

paragraphs: Generative reward models produce critiques and preference judgments, but training often rewards only whether the final preference label is correct. The authors show that this can reward a guessed answer even when its critique is unsound. As a result, the training signal can fail to distinguish good evaluative reasoning from a lucky outcome.

RM-NLHF uses human-written feedback to provide a reward for the critique itself. It measures similarity between a generated critique and a human critique, adding a process-level signal beyond final-label correctness. This gives training information about the explanation supporting a judgment, addressing the ambiguity of binary outcome rewards.

Because collecting human critiques at scale is difficult, the authors introduce MetaRM. It learns to predict process rewards from examples with human critiques and applies that learned capability to data without them. Across multiple benchmarks, RM-NLHF consistently outperforms state-of-the-art models trained with outcome rewards. The results support the value of richer natural-language feedback for training reward models in the evaluated settings.
icml-2026-reward-modeling-from-natural-l.tldr: RM-NLHF trains reward models using critique-level human feedback, with MetaRM extending process rewards to examples lacking human critiques.

paragraphs: Vision-language-action models must connect visual understanding and language-based reasoning to physical control. This paper identifies two obstacles to deployment: high-level reasoning becomes entangled with low-level control, and policy optimization can be unstable. SyVLA is a model trained with diversified experiences to address these connected problems.

Its Intention Decoupling algorithm separates features relevant to control from the surrounding reasoning context. This targets the relationship between understanding a task and selecting actions. A second component uses similar samples to guide reinforcement learning, aiming to stabilize policy updates and reduce the effects of distribution shift. The two components address representation and training stability together.

Experiments cover real-world robotic tasks and multimodal benchmarks. The authors report higher task success rates and stronger generalization outside the training distribution than existing methods, while preserving the model’s core vision-language capabilities. Those findings matter because improving action performance should coexist with the understanding abilities that support it. The evidence supports that combination across the evaluated tasks and benchmarks.
icml-2026-scaling-by-diversified-experie.tldr: SyVLA separates control features from reasoning context and stabilizes reinforcement learning to improve robotic success and generalization.

paragraphs: Encouraging a language model to reason longer does not necessarily guide it toward correct conclusions. This paper investigates how truth-related information appears inside unfolding reasoning chains and how internal representations can be edited to influence their direction. The authors find sentence-level truth signals entangled with different reasoning patterns.

Their analysis also indicates that useful intervention should target early, uncertain branching points, and that noisy steering directions can damage trajectories that were already correct. DynaSteer responds by clustering reasoning patterns and using Fisher linear discriminant analysis to isolate cleaner truth-related directions. It then monitors lookahead entropy to decide when intervention is warranted.

The framework selectively steers reasoning and rolls trajectories back when needed, making the intervention depend on the evolving reasoning state. Experiments on several MATH benchmarks demonstrate effectiveness, while coding experiments provide evidence of transfer outside the original domain. These findings support selective representation editing as a way to guide reasoning, without implying that an internal truth signal guarantees correct answers.
icml-2026-search-for-truth-from-reasonin.tldr: DynaSteer selectively edits internal representations at uncertain reasoning branches to improve mathematical reasoning and transfer to coding tasks.

paragraphs: Multimodal language models can produce text that does not match the image and text they receive. This paper examines an architectural contributor: causal attention in decoder-only models prevents earlier tokens from incorporating information from later ones. When image tokens precede text tokens, the image representation cannot attend to that later text.

Modality-mutual attention changes this access pattern so image tokens can attend to text tokens. This allows visual processing within the model to incorporate information from the accompanying language. The modification addresses communication between modalities inside the attention mechanism, without adding model parameters. It therefore targets a different part of the system from specialized connectors or additional visual instruction tuning.

The authors report state-of-the-art results on 12 multimodal understanding benchmarks, with an average improvement of 6.2% across three language-model backbones. These results support the usefulness of changing cross-modal attention access. The design is intended to extend to other modalities and multimodal settings; that broader applicability is presented as a design aim beyond the reported evaluations.
icml-2026-seeing-is-understanding-unlock.tldr: Modality-mutual attention lets image tokens attend to text tokens, improving multimodal understanding without adding parameters.

paragraphs: Guiding diffusion generation toward a task objective often requires repeated derivative or score evaluations. URGE replaces this guidance-weight computation with a trajectory-based procedure. It assigns a multiplicative importance weight to each simulated path and periodically resamples trajectories, using a Girsanov change of measure to define those weights.

The method connects two ways of organizing sequential Monte Carlo: weighting entire paths and weighting particles at individual stages. The authors establish that a backward conditional expectation of the path weight recovers the earlier particle-level weights. Their equivalence result shows that both schemes produce the same unbiased terminal law, providing a theoretical basis for the simpler path-based construction.

The proposed weighting procedure requires no score, Hessian, or partial-differential-equation evaluation and is described as fully gradient-free. On synthetic tests and diffusion-model benchmarks, URGE produces better generation quality than the tested inference-time guidance baselines. The contribution combines that empirical improvement with a simpler implementation and a formal account of how its trajectory weights relate to particle-based guidance.
icml-2026-simple-approximation-and-deriv.tldr: URGE guides diffusion sampling through derivative-free trajectory weighting and resampling, with a theoretical link to unbiased particle-based schemes.

paragraphs: Long-context attention is expensive because its computation grows quadratically with sequence length. Block-sparse methods reduce work by skipping groups of attention entries, but their efficiency depends on where important entries fall. A small number of useful key tokens scattered across many blocks can still force computation over numerous mostly unnecessary entries.

Permuted Block-Sparse Attention changes token arrangement using attention’s permutation properties to increase sparsity at the block level. The central idea is that useful attention relationships can occupy fewer blocks after rearrangement. This makes more block computation avoidable and targets the prefilling stage, when the model processes an input prompt.

The method is designed as a plug-and-play component and is supported by custom permuted-FlashAttention kernels. Across challenging long-context datasets, it consistently improves accuracy over the compared block-sparse approaches while remaining close to full attention. The authors report end-to-end prefilling speedups of up to 2.75 times. The findings show that block arrangement, alongside which relationships are retained, matters for practical sparse-attention efficiency.
icml-2026-sparser-block-sparse-attention.tldr: PBS-Attn rearranges tokens to concentrate useful attention into fewer blocks, accelerating long-context prefilling while closely matching full-attention accuracy.

paragraphs: With a constant learning step size, stochastic approximation typically settles into a stationary distribution of iterates. Earlier Gaussian-limit results describe what happens as the step size approaches zero, but do not give a usable approximation error for a fixed step size. This paper supplies explicit bounds for that practical setting.

The analysis covers stochastic gradient descent on smooth strongly convex objectives, linear stochastic approximation, and contractive nonlinear updates. It considers both independent noise and temporally dependent Markovian noise. The main results bound the Wasserstein distance between the centered, scaled stationary distribution and its Gaussian limit, explicitly tracking dimension and step size. The bounds vanish as the step size decreases.

The authors also compare stationary tail probabilities with Gaussian tails, with an error term that decreases with deviation level and step size. Their toolkit combines Stein’s method, moment bounds, and Poisson equations for temporal dependence. Extending the analysis to general convex objectives suggests non-Gaussian limiting behavior, supported by numerical experiments rather than asserted as a universal Gaussian approximation.
icml-2026-steady-state-behavior-of-const.tldr: The paper quantifies Gaussian approximation errors and tail behavior for stationary stochastic approximation at fixed step sizes.

paragraphs: Self-rewarding language models generate responses, judge them, and learn from preferred-versus-rejected pairs. The authors identify a weakening training signal: as both kinds of response improve together, their representations become less distinct. Preference optimization then has less contrast to learn from across successive training rounds.

Temporal Self-Rewarding Language Models construct the two sides of a preference pair using different model generations. Anchored Rejection keeps rejected responses tied to outputs from the initial model. Future-Guided Chosen selects preferred examples using next-generation predictions. This temporal separation is designed to sustain useful differences between the examples that training favors and those it rejects.

Experiments across Llama, Qwen, and Mistral show improvements over self-rewarding with the same computational resources. For Llama3.1-8B, AlpacaEval 2.0 win rate rises from 19.69 to 29.44. The method also improves generalization on mathematics, knowledge-based question answering, and coding without specifically collecting training data for those tasks. Extensions to online reinforcement learning for mathematical reasoning provide further evidence for the temporal strategy.
icml-2026-temporal-self-rewarding-langua.tldr: Temporal self-rewarding preserves preference-learning contrast by anchoring rejected answers in an earlier model and selecting preferred answers with later predictions.

paragraphs: Reconstructing biological dynamics from limited observations requires accounting for both movement through a state space and changes in mass. Dynamic unbalanced optimal transport provides a framework for these coupled effects. Existing approaches, however, can make prediction expensive by simulating trajectories during inference.

The proposed mean-flow framework summarizes transport and mass growth over arbitrary time intervals using mean velocity and mean growth fields. These summaries enable generation in a single step without simulating the intervening trajectory. WFR-MFM builds on this construction to solve dynamic unbalanced transport under Wasserstein–Fisher–Rao geometry, retaining both movement and mass variation in the modeled evolution.

Across synthetic datasets and real single-cell RNA sequencing data, the authors report inference that is orders of magnitude faster than a range of baselines while maintaining high predictive accuracy. They also demonstrate efficient perturbation-response prediction on large synthetic datasets containing thousands of conditions. The results support interval-level summaries as a way to make these dynamical predictions substantially cheaper at inference time.
icml-2026-wfr-mfm-one-step-inference-for.tldr: WFR-MFM summarizes movement and mass growth over time intervals to enable fast, one-step prediction of unbalanced dynamics.

paragraphs: Zero-Flow Encoders adapts ideas from flow-based generation to learning informative representations. Its starting point is a precise mathematical criterion: for a rectified flow trained with independent coupling, the flow is zero everywhere at the midpoint exactly when the source and target distributions are identical. The independent-coupling setting is part of the stated result.

The authors show how this zero-flow criterion can certify conditional independence. That connection lets the framework identify representations containing sufficient information from the data. The contribution moves from comparing distributions to determining whether a learned representation retains the information needed for the relevant conditional relationships.

To make the idea usable in training, the paper derives a tractable loss that does not require simulation. It applies this loss to learning amortized Markov blankets in graphical models and latent representations for self-supervised learning. Experiments on simulated and real-world datasets demonstrate effectiveness. Together, these results establish a route from a distribution-equality criterion to practical representation-learning objectives.
icml-2026-zero-flow-encoders-f6d1f80c9b.tldr: Zero-Flow Encoders turns a midpoint flow criterion for distribution equality into a simulation-free objective for learning sufficient representations.
